back.body: MEDICAL inverts TRAUMA · The story tells you more than your hands do · Scene safety + primary assessment FIRST regardless · RESPONSIVE: OPQRST + SAMPLE, then a focused exam aimed by the history · UNRESPONSIVE: rapid head-to-toe + vitals first, history from family, bottles, the room · Reassess 5 min unstable / 15 min stable
back.why_it_matters: The refrigerator full of insulin is history nobody asked for.

back.body: Chief complaint = what the PATIENT says, quoted · Never write your impression in that field · Common: chest pain, SOB, altered mental status, abdominal pain, weakness, dizziness, syncope, nausea/vomiting · VAGUE COMPLAINTS IN OLDER PATIENTS ARE HIGH RISK — cardiac events, sepsis and GI bleeds all present as 'just weak' · The complaint starts the questioning, it does not name the system
back.why_it_matters: Write 'anxiety attack' and every person after you reads your guess instead of her symptom.
